_note: Fictional workplace scenarios. 'mode_used' asks about the behaviour of the person the scenario describes. stakes/relationship/urgency describe the situation for the security champion.

S01.text: The orders team lead insists the SQL injection fix in the internal admin tool waits until next quarter and refuses to discuss it. You feel the tension in every stand-up.

S02.text: The partner API's product owner ignores three emails about a TLS certificate that expires in two days and skips the meeting you booked. Friction is growing.

S03.text: You and the QA lead disagree on test data. You run a joint workshop to explore options for masking production data so both teams' goals are met.

S04.text: After a two-week debate the ops and app teams are polarised. Ops offers to split the work: patch half of the servers now and the rest next month.

S05.text: A junior developer, irritation showing, gives in to keep the peace and agrees to drop the input-validation story the product owner called gold-plating.

S06.text: The gateway lead insisted that only the gateway should do authorization. The two leads now recruit allies among managers and people are taking sides.

S07.text: The infra lead disabled a WAF rule that broke a partner integration. He went ahead without approval, a fait accompli: 'my way or no release'.

S08.text: The release manager sends an ultimatum: sign the pen-test risk exception by 5 pm or else he escalates to the CTO and names you as the blocker.

S09.text: After the dev manager's public blame of security at the all-hands, the security lead stays silent and changes the subject in every later meeting.

S10.text: You disagree with the designer about the colour of the security dashboard. You say 'whatever you prefer' and go along with it.

S11.text: There is some friction over log redaction. The SRE team proposes to pair with you and co-design the redaction filter around a shared goal.

S12.text: The vendor and your procurement team are talking past each other on the security SLA. They meet in the middle: slower fix times for medium issues, a lower price.
